clue.text: Distress in hearing — stop being crooked

indicators.note: something heard rather than read is judged by its sound, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase that follows

parts.note: to stop being crooked is to become straight again, and the spelling here is the narrow-strait version

explanation.surface: Someone in pain from an ear problem is begging a twisted person to go straight.
explanation.walkthrough: STRAIGHTEN and STRAITEN sound identical; the second, related to strait and straitened circumstances, is the one defined.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to put someone in hardship or difficulty, especially financial, which is a form of causing distress.

clue.text: Small amount of time with Bill

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
a bill is an advertisement, shortened to ad

explanation.surface: A brief moment spent with a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name but is a poster or advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tad is a colloquial word for a little bit or a slight quantity of something.

clue.text: Hates playing brag — turned out friends accepting bluff directly

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being toyed with and moved around rather than left in order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
to crow is to boast or brag

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another
to turn out a room or pocket is to empty it, so only the shell of the word is kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of friends
a bluff is a deception, a lie

explanation.surface: A card game of brag goes sour and friends are told off for bluffing; brag is a British gambling card game like poker.
explanation.walkthrough: Brag looks like the card game of the surface, but it is a verb meaning boast. The answer is a phrase meaning by the shortest route.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes the straight-line distance between two points, so it means by the most direct route.

clue.text: Start old games console — knob needed to spin around

parts.note: to turn on a machine is to start it
O is a common abbreviation for old
the NES is the Nintendo Entertainment System, an early home games console
knob is British slang for an unpleasant idiot, and a heel is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Instructions for firing up a retro games machine, which apparently needs a dial twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: Old looks like it describes the console, but it supplies its own letter before NES.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on one's heel is the idiom for abruptly pivoting and walking away, which is spinning around.

clue.text: New supermarket stops Marmite supply — almost!

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other
read as supple-y, in a flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged; Marmite is a British yeast spread
Asda is a large British supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A newly opened shop halts its supply of Marmite, nearly causing a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Supply looks like a noun but is read as an adverb, meaning flexibly. The supermarket sits inside the jumbled spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Near as dammit is an informal British phrase meaning very nearly, so close that the difference hardly matters.

clue.text: One of your relatives gift wraps a book!

indicators.note: wrapping something means putting a covering around it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a boon is a blessing or gift
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for book

explanation.surface: A family member hands over a present they have wrapped, a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cheeky one: as primates, apes and monkeys are humans' distant relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Baboons are monkeys, primates sharing ancestry with humans, so jokingly one of your kin.

clue.text: Number 24 buses do use buckles

indicators.note: something that buckles bends out of shape, so these letters are distorted into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 24, the second part of the phrase at 4
the remaining letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bus route numbered 24 runs along roads where something gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 24 looks like a bus route, but Number alone is the definition and 24 points to another answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a song or piece of music, and this is the rock and roll song by Carl Perkins made famous by Elvis Presley.

clue.text: Lancashire landmark seen when Cilla, say takes in middle of Bolton

parts.note: Cilla Black was a Liverpool singer and TV presenter

indicators.note: taking something in means admitting it inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: having a say in a matter means having power or influence over it

indicators.note: only the central part of the following word is kept, discarding its ends

parts.note: the inner letters of Bolton, losing the first and last

explanation.surface: A northern landmark comes into view when a celebrity singer passes through Bolton, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Say looks like it means for example, attached to Cilla, but it is a noun: a say is a voice in a decision, so POWER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian iron tower on the seafront at the resort of Blackpool is one of the county's best-known sights.

clue.text: 10 deliveries brought up under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means being written below it, so this piece comes after

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
P is the abbreviation for pressure
children brought up are raised

explanation.surface: A cricket team's bowling was brought up for discussion while they were under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliveries suggests post or childbirth, but here it is cricket: an over is six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer to 10 means complimented to excess, and overpraised says exactly that: praised too much.

clue.text: Journalist: Balls maybe yellow after sex

indicators.note: after places the word before it later in the answer than the word that follows it

parts.note: Ed Balls is a British former Labour politician and broadcaster
it is a coy word for sex
or is the heraldic term for gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporter writes about cowardly behaviour following a sex scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls maybe points to a person named Balls; yellow, though it looks like cowardice, is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior newspaper person in charge of content, and so a kind of journalist.

clue.text: Excessively complimented pornographic actor's first lines — 9 must be abbreviated

indicators.note: as a verb, to line something is to sit inside it as a lining

parts.note: adult is the euphemism for pornographic material

indicators.note: first tells us to keep only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of actor
the answer at 9 is commonly shortened to ed

explanation.surface: Instructions for a pornographic film script: the lead's opening lines must be cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: Lines looks like dialogue but is a verb: the letter lines the word, sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or admire someone excessively, so adulated means praised beyond measure.

clue.text: Ordnance Survey cutting about page in misprinted A-to-Z — it's a gem

indicators.note: something cutting into a word splits it apart and sits in the gap
in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
OS is the abbreviation for Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency

indicators.note: a misprint puts characters in the wrong places, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged; an A-to-Z is a British street atlas
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A map-maker notices a printing error on a page of a street atlas and calls it a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: The map references dominate the surface, but only the abbreviation OS and the letters of A-to-Z are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose topaz is a pink variety of the precious stone, so it is a kind of gemstone.

clue.text: Touching article cast read aloud for sovereign

parts.note: on means in contact with, touching
the definite article

indicators.note: reading words out loud means we want something that sounds like the word before it

parts.note: cast means thrown, which is pronounced the same as the royal seat

explanation.surface: An actor in a touching drama reads aloud a part written for a king.
explanation.walkthrough: Cast suggests actors, but it is the past tense of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who is reigning is said to be on the throne, so the phrase means holding sovereign power.

clue.text: Misses sleep on board ship

indicators.note: to be on board a vessel is to be inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: A passenger misses out by sleeping through a voyage on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS, steamship, is a standard crossword way of boxing a word in.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to miss it out or omit it, as in skipping a class.

clue.text: See 6
Unknown firm taken on by heavyweight businessman

indicators.note: being taken on by something means being taken into it, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a ton is a great weight
y is one of the algebraic unknowns
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: An obscure company is acquired by a big-shot business figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Heavyweight looks like a powerful person, but it is simply a large weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy and powerful figure in business or industry, a magnate.

clue.text: See 3
Dawn French to the rescue — often raising awareness for starters

parts.note: au is French for to the

indicators.note: starters are the opening parts, so the first letters of the preceding words are taken

parts.note: the initial letters of the four words

explanation.surface: The comedian Dawn French comes to the rescue, campaigning for a cause; she is a well-known British comic actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn French is a single famous name, but the clue splits it: Dawn is the definition and French starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the Latin name and poetic word for daybreak, personified as the Roman goddess of the morning.

clue.text: Former opponent gutted about discharged cruise missile

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped around the other
gutting removes the insides, leaving just the outer shell of the word

parts.note: the first and last letters of opponent

indicators.note: discharged means emptied of its load, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of cruise

explanation.surface: A defeated former enemy is said to have fired a cruise missile.
explanation.walkthrough: Cruise missile reads as one phrase, but cruise belongs to the wordplay and missile alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exocet is a French-built anti-ship guided missile, made famous in the Falklands War.

clue.text: Goes off instruction to make nice e-readers?

parts.note: surface reading: a how-to for building pleasant electronic book readers
setter's reading: nice is KIND, and the instruction says what to tack on to turn it into the brand name of Amazon's e-readers

explanation.surface: A gadget guide's instructions for building pleasant e-book readers go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: KIND (nice) becomes KINDLES (Amazon's e-readers) if you ADD LES, and that instruction, run together, is ADDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs or food that addle go rotten or spoil, which is what going off means.

clue.text: See 5
Dislodge key

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to move something from its place
second meaning: the keyboard key used for capitals

explanation.walkthrough: Key suggests a lock, but it is a computer keyboard key.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for moving something along and the name of the keyboard key that switches to capital letters.

clue.text: Lad struggling with issue including, ultimately, combat fatigue

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one piece sits within the other
struggling suggests thrashing about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, part of the jumble
taken as written, part of the jumble

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the final letter of combat

explanation.surface: A young soldier struggling with a problem ends up suffering from battle fatigue.
explanation.walkthrough: Combat fatigue looks like one term, but only fatigue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is a state of physical or mental weariness and lack of energy, which is tiredness.

clue.text: See 7
See 4
E.coli must, mostly, spread in bowl

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
spread suggests being scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the full stop
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A food-safety warning that bacteria must be spreading in a mixing bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowl looks like kitchenware, but it is a sports stadium, like the Hollywood Bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A coliseum is a large stadium or amphitheatre, and a bowl is another word for an arena of that shape.

clue.text: Bond villain, Jaws essentially breaking back to get ahead

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the result is read from right to left
breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is inserted

parts.note: Dr No is the villain of the first James Bond film

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the central letters are kept

parts.note: the middle letters of Jaws, another Bond henchman

explanation.surface: Two James Bond baddies, with the steel-toothed Jaws breaking his back, try to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaws is also a Bond villain, which makes it look like a second definition, but only its core is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Onward means forward or further ahead, as in moving onward to the next stage.

clue.text: Premier Cru can finally flow

indicators.note: finally points to the end of each of the preceding words, so their last letters are kept

parts.note: the closing letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A fine wine from a can is at last allowed to pour out.
explanation.walkthrough: Premier Cru is a top French wine classification, and the can is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquids that run are moving freely in a stream, so the verb means to flow.

clue.text: Ship leaves Selsey after dropping off some bits

indicators.note: dropping some letters from each end leaves a run of letters inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words; Selsey is a seaside town in West Sussex

explanation.surface: A boat departs from a south-coast harbour after unloading part of its cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like a verb of departure, but it is just the start of the letter string.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is any ship or boat, a craft that travels on water.

clue.text: Volunteers, once in the forces, not against shocking treatment?

parts.note: the Territorial Army was Britain's volunteer reserve force before being renamed the Army Reserve

indicators.note: not means without, so the following word's letter is removed

parts.note: someone in the forces is serving
v is short for versus, against

explanation.surface: Former army reservists object to receiving shocking treatment in the forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a pun: tasering is a treatment that delivers a literal electric shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a Taser stun gun on someone delivers an electric shock, so the activity is treatment that literally shocks.
